speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: It was amended in 2007 to provide a legislative framework for the liberalisation of the Postal Services sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Since then, market and technological changes, especially the rise of e-commerce, have transformed the postal landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The existing letterbox infrastructure is not designed for parcel delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: And the current market for locker infrastructure is fragmented and unable to support projected growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Self-collection parcel lockers are also currently concentrated in high-traffic commercial areas catering to only 5% of total parcel volume and leaving residential areas under served.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: These parcel lockers, which are operated by individual DSPs are also not accessible to other operators, resulting in a fragmented market and infrastructure duplication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: We carefully considered the options available in arriving at the solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Currently, SingPost is the only public postal licensee, or PPL, and this arrangement has served us well in a time where the postal service was used predominantly for the conveyance of letter mail.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The rise of e-commerce and a multitude of players in the logistics sector innovating and seeking to deliver value to consumers have ushered in a different era.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The vibrant last mile delivery sector has thrived with open and free competition and should be given room to flourish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: It is therefore our priority to facilitate an environment where all players can participate equitably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: An open access nationwide parcel locker network, or Network for short, which any DSP and e-commerce marketplace can use will provide greater convenience and options for parcel deliveries while complementing the existing letterbox infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This will ensure the neutrality of the Network and also allow it to be freely accessible to the industry and all consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: At this point, Sir, I would like to assure the House that it is not our intent for Pick to compete with DSPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Pick is solely an infrastructure provider and operator and will not be involved in the conveyance of parcels, which is the core business of DSPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Instead, Pick will give DSPs more options for the last mile delivery of parcels and increase their productivity and efficiency with fewer missed doorstep deliveries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Network also includes an interoperability platform, which private locker operators can be part of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Further, any DSP is welcome to use Pick's lockers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Pick has been working with all these partners to come on board the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This will ensure open and fair access to Pick's lockers, provide an opportunity for individual operators to extend their reach beyond their own parcel lockers and help level the playing field in the parcel last mile delivery market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: We are one of the first countries in the world with a nation wide open access locker network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: In this Bill, we seek to introduce a regulatory framework which would facilitate the deployment of the network in a timely fashion as well as ensure the safety and security of the network In addition, while the Network is operated by an IMDA subsidiary, there will be regulatory oversight of the Network and Pick under the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Bill also takes into consideration feedback from consultations with industry and the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: For example, a key change made was to allow the public to return their items at the Network's lockers at HDB estates and Community Centres and Clubs for greater convenience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This widens options for consumers and saves time and trouble.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Second, level the playing field for the parcel last mile delivery market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Third, support the continuity of postal services by ensuring the provision and maintenance of letterbox infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: And fourth, streamline and clarify existing provisions in the PSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The first set of amendments pertains to the Network while the other amendments address operational issues related to postal services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: First, amendments related to the deployment of the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Clause 3 amends section 3A to set out IMDA's functions and duties with regard to the Network, which include ensuring that the Network is accessible, reliable, secure, affordable to use and well-regulated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Today, IMDA as the postal authority, is conferred the exclusive privilege in relation to conveying letters and performing all related incidental services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The new section 23B gives IMDA the exclusive privilege of establishing, installing, operating and maintaining the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As a safeguard against any failure by the appointed operator to comply with the relevant provisions of the amended PSA or any conditions imposed by IMDA, the new section 23D allows IMDA to establish, install, operate and maintain the Network or any part of the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Given that space in public areas is already limited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Specified premises includes the public places where the public parcel lockers previously announced by my Ministry will be located.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The new sections 23M to 22O allow IMDA to issue codes of practice, written notices and written directions concerning the provision of an access to space for the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Non-compliance with any such written notices or written directions without reasonable cause is an offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Respondents to the public consultation on the draft Bill raised concerns on the safety and security of the Network, citing the possibility of hazardous materials and illicit items being placed into the Network's lockers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: For example, IMDA will have the powers to direct the network operator to search the Network's lockers and to detain any suspected harmful items found in them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: If any item in the Network's lockers is suspected to pose a threat to public security or public health, the Police and authorised IMDA officers will have the power to search the Network's lockers and seize the item.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: It will also be an offence for any person to place a prohibited item as specified under the amended PSA in Pick's lockers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Other offences are introduced to protect the Network and ensure the security and integrity of parcels being delivered into the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: For instance, the new sections 39B and 39E make it an offence to damage or tamper with the Network to intercept or obstruct the delivery or collection of parcels, and to wilfully remove, destroy or damage the Network's lockers or related installations or related software.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Under the new section 39H, officers, employees, agents or contractors of the Network operator or a DSP may also be penalised with a fine and/or jail term if they destroy, steal or throw away parcels in Pick's lockers, or wilfully open or cause to be opened parcels or lockers without authorisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Some industry players have requested access to the letterboxes to deliver e-commerce items which can fit into existing letterboxes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: We consider this to be reasonable, as wholesale access to letterboxes for letters is already in place today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Regulating wholesale access for the delivery of non-letter items also complements the introduction of the Network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This will allow other industry players to have access to letterboxes, and provide consumers and the industry with more choices in the receipt and last-mile delivery of parcels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The amended section 24 will enable IMDA to regulate such wholesale access through codes of practice or standards of performance, including rates and charges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This will ensure that charges are fair and that consumers will ultimately benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: While the digital economy has changed the way we live, work and play, postal services still play a key role in communications and the conveyance of goods through the postal network, supported by a letterbox infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Today, under section 16 of the PSA, building developers are required to provide letterboxes before a building is handed over to its owner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: However, it is unclear which party is responsible for replacing letterboxes which are damaged or in need of repair, or providing additional letterboxes when a lot within a building is subdivided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Clause 8 amends section 16 to provide greater clarity on the provision and maintenance of letterboxes by introducing obligations on building managers, referred to as "applicable persons" in the Bill, to ensure that there will be no lapses in the delivery of letters due to inadequate letterbox infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Clause 4 amends section 5 such that persons providing an intra-organisational mail-room service or a messenger service are not required to obtain a licence under the PSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This is in recognition of the fact that both are business support services with a narrower scope of activity than what licensed Postal Services Operators offer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Mail handling by such services is also not the core business of an organisation and mail volumes are typically low, at around fewer than 50 pieces a day, compared to the three million mail items that SingPost handles daily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This amendment will reduce regulatory obligations on companies with such services and aligns Singapore with other jurisdictions such as the UK, which does not license such services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Clause 6 amends section 11 to clarify that only specified PPLs authorised under their licences may provide for the postal remittance of money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Similarly, clause 10 amends section 19 in relation to the issuance of postal stamps bearing the word "Singapore".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: These amendments cater to a scenario where there is more than one PPL.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Section 45 of the PSA allows the Minister to issue directions to any postal licensee in relation to the exercise of the licensee's functions under the PSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As e-commerce is a sector that looks set for further growth, these amendments are timely and will put us in good stead to capture opportunities in the digital future.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: During the circuit breaker period last year, there was a sharp decline in face-to-face social interactions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: As a result, many had resorted to purchasing parcels and gifts online to be couriered to friends and/or extended family as a means of keeping in touch with them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We also witnessed an increase in purchases made through e-commerce platforms, for work-from-home equipment such as monitors, desks, chairs and so on, and also essential items and groceries for household needs and use.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: If not for the instrumental role that the postmen and last mile delivery personnel played then and continue to play today, we would not have been able to receive our purchases and/or parcels from our friends and loved ones in a timely fashion.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: However, as circuit breaker measures were lifted, and people started commuting more, there was a corresponding increase in failed doorstep deliveries.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This has practical implications for the logistics services' providers as repeated deliveries have to be made, which is a drain on both time and resources.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: For recipients of the parcels, they would be inconvenienced if they needed the items urgently.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On my end, I also faced an issue for such deliveries.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Just last month, my family had purchased a product from an online seller which cost less than $50.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It was for an urgent use and we even paid for a special delivery package by SingPost for the item to be delivered to my home.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On the day of expected shipment, even though the parcel was tagged and traced as delivered and I received a notification on the delivery, we eventually did not receive the item from SingPost.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We contacted the seller and he said he checked and SingPost said they had delivered.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I then had to contact SingPost to inform them that we did not receive the item and that it was for urgent use.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The investigation took more than three days and we had to go ahead to make a repurchase due to the urgency.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On the fourth day, we were told by SingPost that their postman had mailed the product to the wrong address.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There was little recourse for me, as the seller who had paid SingPost to carry out the delivery was supposed to be the correct party to file a complaint and/or claim with SingPost, even though I had already paid the seller for the product.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Legally, I needed to file a claim with the seller who in turn needed to counterclaim with SingPost for the negligent act.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The multiple parties and various payments involved in this transaction made the recovery of that product or any ensuing claims a cumbersome exercise.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I did not pursue the matter and I just had to settle with two sets of the same product.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I believe I am not the only one faced with such a problem.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Some online companies or platforms do a better job by not releasing funds to the seller until the buyer receives the item.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Such is the nature and challenge for e-commerce and online purchases.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: With the Network, postmen and delivery persons will deposit the parcels directly at the Network, for residents' collection at their convenience.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: While the Bill is no doubt commendable, I have some queries for the Minister, which may be broadly categorised into the following areas.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: One, security issues associated with the Network; two, convenience and/or public policy matters; and three, employment issues arising from the development of the Network.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: From a security perspective, how would the Network be implemented?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Would the Minister be able to share some of the technological safeguards in place to ensure that the parcel is not tampered with, given that multiple service providers have access to the same parcel box?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Perhaps we could consider the installation of additional CCTVs?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: These are security issues which are less prevalent in the context of traditional letter boxes, where postmen simply slot letters into the letter boxes and only residents who have the keys to their letter boxes can collect the said letters.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Additionally, in cases of pilfering, be it by delivery personnel, pranksters and/or others who have access to the parcel boxes, who shall be liable for such losses and what recourse do the rightful owners have?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Further, we also note that certain prescribed classes of parcels will be prohibited from being placed in the Network for safety reasons.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: While there are powers conferred upon the Network Operator, the Police and IMDA to search, open and seize such parcels, however, how shall this be monitored and/or enforced practically, given that most of the parcels are usually packaged before being delivered?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We need to ensure the safety of our postmen, last mile delivery personnel and residents who deliver and collect such parcels.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Next, the Network is presently to be established at HDB estates and/or public areas.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Some private estates and condominiums are within proximity to HDB Housing estates and some may be keen to have these parcel boxes in their own precincts.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Third, employment issues arising from the development of the Network.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: From an employment perspective, while I am confident that the Network will make the jobs of our postmen as well as last mile delivery personnel less strenuous due to failed and repeated deliveries, it will also bring about a fresh set of challenges for our postmen and delivery personnel, such as adapting to technological advancements like enhanced tracking, electronic signatures and so on, and picking up new skill sets to multi-task and multi-skill.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am also particularly concerned about the wages, the welfare and work prospects of these postal and delivery personnel, in particular, the overall attractiveness of this sector which continues to play a crucial role as we navigate the pandemic, thrive in the next normal of a low touch economy and grapple with an ageing population.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Sometimes, deliveries get delayed because residents are not at home to receive the parcel, or they do not hear the courier at the door.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will require rescheduling to another delivery date.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I also remember occasions when I would receive a delivery note in my mailbox to pick up a package from a POPStation, which is a 30-minute round trip by bus and foot from my home, when I had made it a point to be home when the original delivery was made.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The pandemic, ironically, seems to have ease this problem, because couriers, now simply leave the package outside the door in the name of contactless delivery to prevent the spread of the virus.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, I worry that these delivery issues may return once safe management measures ease.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In any case, especially in public housing estates, leaving packages unattended at the door risks parcel theft.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I therefore support the plan to situate more parcel lockers near housing estates.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, I have several queries which I hope that Senior Minister of State will address.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These cover the effect of the creation of public parcel locker network on market competition and innovation and the coverage of parcel lockers in all housing estates.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Pick is a wholly owned subsidiary of IMDA, a which is a Government Statutory board.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: SingPost currently has POPStations, and Blu World Pte Ltd has a network of blue lockers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They are part of an existing parcel local network, the Locker Alliance, which has already set up parcel lockers in various locations across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They already have the experience of running parcel lockers and could take on the investment risk and bear the cost of expanding the network.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is Pick's mandate to fulfil a need that is distinct and complementary to the services already provided by the private parcel locker providers, or will it be competing with them?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If competition is part of this mandate, will it be contravening the Yellow Pages rule?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This rule dictates that Government agencies should exit from market segments, which already have active private sector players.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note that Senior Minister of State said that it is not the Bill's intent for Pick to compete with delivery service partners, but does this non-competition extend to providers of parcel lockers?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Going back to first principles, I would like to find out more information about the process by which Pick was created and contracted to run the network.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Are there plans for a subsequent tender, in which another public postal licensee or licensees can participate in?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is Pick expected to be profitable in future?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Next, I have some questions for the Senior Minister of State about the location and coverage of the network lockers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: While residents living in HDB estates will be served by the Network, how will the Network be implemented in condominiums and landed estates if at all?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will parcel lockers be set up in condominiums or in public spaces near condominiums?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given that 16% of resident households live in condominiums, we should strive to ensure coverage of this segment.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Another five percent of residents live in landed housing.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will they be served by public parcel lockers?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Next, I understand that Pick will be in charge of the maintenance of these lockers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given the COVID-19 situation, Pick should arrange for their own disinfection and cleaning of the high touch surfaces of these lockers regularly.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Also, I hope that Pick clearly indicates that customer support contacts on their lockers and makes it convenient for customers to get in touch with them.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is so, that Town Councils or Members of Parliament do not get calls from members of the public to fix malfunctioning lockers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: There may also be certain individuals who are heavy users of delivery services – for example, people who run small redistribution businesses from their homes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What measures are in place to prevent overuse by these individuals who could end up monopolising the limited slots?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It should seek to drive innovation in the sector, for example, perhaps in future we could see the creation of cold lockers to facilitate the delivery of groceries and foodstuffs from supermarkets, or heated lockers for food deliveries.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Locker operators could also consider providing dual functions for their lockers, for example, as receptacles for return items or even depositing electronic waste, given that existing e-waste bins are even less accessible then private parcel lockers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The creation of the Network should ultimately drive the industry forward and serve the public interest, given that public funds have already been used towards this creation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: ROI must come in the form of more convenient and affordable parcel pick up for consumers; not just profits for a select few players, whether publicly or privately owned.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such lockers offer an additional mode of delivery to busy Singaporeans and residents who prefer to pick up their items in their own time and not have to wait for their deliveries at designated places as they may be on the move.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How does IMDA ensure that no hazardous materials will be sent via the Network?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share with us the security process undertaken by the vendors?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, the bulk of these deliveries are transacted online.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How do the vendors protect its customers' data from cyber threats, for example, hacking of their databases?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Also, how can the vendors ensure the security of the deliveries, so that the items can reach the intended recipients?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Had there been incidents where the locker systems were breached and thieves were able to make off with any parcels?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, will it be possible to indicate elderly- and disabled-friendly lockers which are positioned at the appropriate height levels so that recipients can choose to have their parcels sent to such lockers?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Most parcels are ordered through online transactions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How will vendors protect the customers’ data from internet threats?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Have there been any incidents of parcel locker systems being damaged or stolen from?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Due to our rapidly ageing population, we must ensure that we consider the needs of the elderly from the design stage, such as installing usage instruction guides in big fonts near the parcel lockers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): Sir, I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What makes these numbers worth mentioning is that they are the numbers reported by Lazada from their 11/11 sale in 2020 for Singapore alone.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The growth of e-commerce has resulted in more deliveries.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Delivery service providers have had to step up to meet the increased volume and maintain service standards throughout the delivery process.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can expect this to be the new norm, moving forward, and hence, the introduction of the Postal Services (Amendment) Bill is a timely one.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is intended to benefit Singaporeans as delivery services will hopefully improve with increased access and reliability.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I have three clarifications to ask the Ministry in this proposed amendment Bill.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Like the hon Member Joan Pereira, firstly, I would like to ask will the parcel lockers have senior and disability friendly features and access, so that our seniors and persons with disabilities can also benefit from the convenience like everyone else?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some specific accessibility considerations can include: (a) placement of touchscreens that are convenient for the wheelchair-bound; (b) pre-selection and designation of certain lockers for the wheelchair-bound, so that they need not worry about not being able to reach the locker for their packages; and (c) to include speech and tactile interfaces for the hearing and visually impaired.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With more seniors aging-in-place, self-management and home-based care for the management of chronic diseases will become increasingly common and the last mile delivery of medication will be useful.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: SingHealth, together with Integrated Health Information System or IHiS for short, have developed their Prescription-In-Locker Box or PILBOX stations to allow patients to collect their medication refills anytime, without having to queue at the polyclinic pharmacies.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While this is a good solution, PILBOX currently is only available at five polyclinics under SingHealth.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second clarification is similar to the hon Member Mr Patrick Tay's concern on how the security of the NPLN be effectively managed?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While no packages were reported lost, the incident highlighted the need to ensure securing both the software and hardware from malicious actors.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I will like to propose to include stronger cybersecurity requirements for the NPLN.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of these requirements could be in the form of cybersecurity-by-design in the software, hardware and infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is to ensure that the cybersecurity best practices are adopted at the very start of the network implementation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Stronger penalties also to be in place specifically for cybersecurity related breaches to encourage operators and service providers to step up in their cybersecurity measures.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And requirements for contingency plans to secure parcel lockers should a security breach happen, resulting in parcel lockers being compromised.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My last clarification is in the area of operating standards and interoperability of the NPLN.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: An open access parcel locker network will make pick-up and drop-off of parcels convenient for Singaporeans as they are not limited to any specific delivery service providers.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would assume that this will require common operating standards, compatible technology platforms or systems which delivery service providers would need to adopt to fully take advantage of the NPLN.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that IMDA’s wholly-owned subsidiary, Pick Network, will ensure that the delivery service providers have fair and open access to the network .

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nonetheless, we will need to be mindful that such an arrangement will not stifle innovation, or worse, create an unintended monopoly by the network operator which may increase the cost of operations for the delivery service providers, especially if they are SME Internet merchants.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also hope that IMDA will allow the delivery service providers and SME Internet merchants to further innovate their solutions and apps on the NPLN for continued last-mile delivery innovations.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The strong adoption of e-commerce by Singaporeans before and during the pandemic has highlighted the need to address inefficiencies, ensure reliability and scalability in last-mile deliveries.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the continued growth of e-commerce, evolving consumer expectations, the Postal Services (Amendment) Bill is a welcome one.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nonetheless, as we put in place the infrastructure for tomorrow, we must not forget the needs of the seniors and persons with disabilities of today.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we build solutions for the future, we cannot afford to ignore the security risks present today.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More importantly, the amendment Bill must prepare Singapore’s logistics network to meet the demands and complexities of the fast-growing e-commerce landscape.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that these efforts and my suggestions can help solidify Singapore as a mature and attractive e-commerce market in Asia.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On that note, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I recall that, back in 2017, when I was still with IBM, the IBM Garage worked with the Singapore start-up, Freshturf, to study the issues from the first-mile to last-mile logistics and to explore technology solutions like blockchain to design the concept of federated locker networks and to create a secure way of making these lockers available to any delivery company wishing to use them.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: While this prototype never got commercialised, Freshturf co-founder Kevin Lim, did share that they learnt much from the prototyping and went on to develop solutions targeted for specific logistics problems.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We have come a long way since 2017 and COVID-19 has accelerated e-commerce even further.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, the Amendment to the Postal Services Act is very timely.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Here are my thoughts on the three key points in the amendment.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The nationwide parcel locker network will transform Singapore’s last-mile delivery infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Two, the PICK lockers will be accessible by all e-commerce and logistics service providers and, in so doing, facilitate competitive pricing and continued innovation of business models, services, regulation and technology adoption.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This will serve to level the playing field for delivery service providers as far as small parcels are concerned.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In my view, another tick mark for this amendment.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In speaking with the Singapore Chamber of E-commerce, we have identified several areas which will still need continued adjustments.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: One, many first- and last-mile operators are not doing well in terms of managing cost.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The wholesale pricing of SingPost and the price of the PICK lockers can potentially help the operators on the cost side and we certainly hope that IMDA and the Government will help facilitate that.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Two, visibility of track and trace data of the packages for the consumers, coupled with the easy access for self-collection at lockers conveniently located near the consumers, will enhance end-user experience.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Three, logistics is a business driven by scale.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We anticipate consolidation in the industry or the development of integrated services hub for urban logistics.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: How does the logistics Industry Transformation Map shape these developments?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Four, security is of increasing importance and, as my hon other Members of Parliament have mentioned ahead of me, how will PICK, SingPOST and IMDA handle the security checks of packages to ensure that there is no mischief?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: How will the PICK platform ensure interoperability with commercial players?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And how will this platform enable our operators to go beyond Singapore?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   I strongly support the Amendment Bill which will empower IMDA to install and manage our nationwide open access parcel locker network.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With the Government in charge of the network, we can better harness the benefits of delivery aggregation and reduce facility duplication from competing private operators in certain locations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is a tremendous boost in productivity and will help solve the problem of manpower shortage in this sector.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It will also greatly reduce our carbon emissions, in line with our environmental goals.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will bring much convenience to our residents.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For the SME suppliers, parcel lockers allow them to consolidate deliveries, which is efficient and save costs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Groceries and temperature-sensitive parcels can be stored in closed, temperature-controlled lockers, which include freezer units.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I share the same hygiene concerns with Member Mr Gerald Giam earlier.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of hygiene.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In some countries, lockers are sanitised with UV light and disinfectant after each use.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would the Minister share the main details about which entity will be responsible for their cleanliness and how standards will be maintained?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am concerned with the security of these locker stations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad that Senior Minister of State Sim Ann has addressed the security-related concerns when she explained the policy intent just now.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Next, what technology will these lockers be equipped with for access?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lockers can be opened with PIN numbers sent by SMS, Whatsapp, QR codes or via Bluetooth with an app on customers’ phones.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need to ensure that everyone, no matter how poor, can access the lockers.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would recommend that we standardise accessibility as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, these lockers should be opened by PIN numbers in case people do not have smartphones, which are necessary for QR codes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On the other hand, with our nationwide push to being a SMART nation, will IMDA be assuming that everyone will be using smartphones?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In some countries, parcel lockers will be used for purposes, such as recycling, particularly, personal electronic devices, consumer-to-consumer sales and delivering rental devices.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In Finland, customers can try on apparel in “fitting room” parcel lockers equipped with digital kiosks.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding the above concerns, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although there is a certain nostalgia associated with receiving handwritten Christmas or Chinese New Year cards, we are now more likely to receive festive greeting GIFs on our mobile phones than physical greeting cards in our mailboxes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the era of Internet-enabled communications and given the ubiquity of online shopping, our postal services need to progress with time.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That being said, we ought to be mindful about potential unintended consequences in IMDA’s implementation of such a nationwide service.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, is there a possibility that a single player will end up dominating the market and, thus, the market is not subject to competitive market forces?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In short, how can we ensure that the service will be affordable for consumers and that this single vendor – should there end up being a single vendor – will also continue to innovate and introduce new services when it is not subjected to competition from other vendors?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Ensuring long-term affordability of such a locker service is important because such a service is an effective alternative solution to door-to-door delivery.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have already heard from some of our colleagues about the challenges of waiting at home to receive some of their parcels and their deliveries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the present moment, door-to-door delivery requires some degree of coordination also between merchants and consumers to ensure that someone is at home.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This results in opportunity cost for consumers in terms of time lost as they must remain at home when their time could have been better spent on other activities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could this lead effectively to the demise of smaller players in the industry and perhaps even affecting door-to-door courier services adversely when demand for such services decline?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would IMDA thus consider working with some of the smaller industry players that might not necessarily run the nationwide network but is still able to contribute to its running in meaningful ways?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Thirdly, since the early 2000s, the Government has tried to minimise the installation of dustbins, for example, in crowded confined spaces, such as MRT stations or bus interchanges, as these receptacles could be used to hide improvised explosive devices (IEDs), which could lead to mass casualties – I am surfacing a point that has been repeated quite a few times already by my other parliamentary colleagues.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, the question is: how would IMDA ensure that the locker service will not be misused by nefarious individuals to hide hazardous biomaterials or IEDs that could cause mass casualties or widespread panic during an incident?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the authorities ensure the safety and security of such a locker system?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My clarifications notwithstanding, I am heartened that the Government has introduced this Postal Services (Amendment) Bill to reflect the consumer landscape of today and conclude my speech in firm support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Most parcels today are delivered to the doorstep.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is convenient, but it comes with its own set of challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Delivery workers are always rushing to meet the deadlines for deliveries.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This can compromise their work quality and safety when rushing from one point to another and parcels are left at the door, with contactless deliveries being encouraged.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, having a better self-collection strategy in place is useful.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is particularly so in the current climate when social distancing is necessary and where there is an increased reliance on delivery services.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We also need to work out the processes to determine if a particular item should go into a locker, mailbox or direct to door.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I will touch on two groups of people who are likely to be more affected by the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we have to cater to homebound residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have many of such residents in Yio Chu Kang who may have difficulties leaving their homes to collect their deliveries.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These include seniors and, especially those with mobility problems.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It also includes care-givers looking after babies and family members with special needs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: One senior in my constituency, Mdm Lim, is homebound due to severe arthritis.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Living alone, she does not leave the house.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: She relies on VWOs for meal deliveries under the Meals-on-Wheels programme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: She seldom checks her letterbox given her immobility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If the parcel station is not under her block, she will have great difficulty retrieving her parcels.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need to make sure that the system caters for such individuals as Mdm Lim.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: During the circuit breaker, when home visitations were not allowed, many of my residents relied on e-commerce.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to help their elderly family members to purchase necessities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Seniors could simply wait at home for their delivery to show up.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In fact, some seniors in my constituency shared with me that they are learning to shop online.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They enjoyed the convenience of door-step delivery so much.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is also a great opportunity to get seniors more comfortable with the use of digital technology.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am concerned that as parcel lockers become more widely available, businesses may find that it is more cost-saving and cease to offer door-step delivery.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some could continue to offer it, but at a much higher cost.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, this may come across as working against the segment of the population that, in fact, stands to benefit most from the convenience of e-commerce.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Savings on labour costs should be passed on to consumers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As parcel lockers are typically accessed digitally, I presume this also applies to the Nationwide Parcel Locker Network.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With the success of the trial in December 2018, will there be any changes to the system by which users retrieve their parcels?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to launch a public awareness campaign as the network progressively expands?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Government ensure that seniors and the less tech-savvy have access to assistance?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be a helpline in case a resident is unable to retrieve their parcel?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Member Patrick Tay has also spoken on this.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Delivery is often cited as a job that is at risk of being automated.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It will not come as a surprise that some delivery workers will find themselves displaced.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many delivery workers may be doing deliveries to supplement their income because their main job does not pay well enough to support their family.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some are in-between jobs, trying to get by as they find more stable employment.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some are care-givers who appreciate the freedom to accept delivery jobs when they can, as micro-jobs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can the transition be made smoother for them?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Does this new infrastructure project offer them opportunities to upskill and move up to a bigger jobscope within the logistics industry?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When logistics service providers have access to well-planned shared infrastructure with the right processes, they provide a more efficient last mile delivery service for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But we must always remember those homebound residents, especially seniors, who have difficulty accessing these lockers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must also remember the challenges faced by delivery workers as a result of this initiative.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This increase, as well as advances in technology, has also led to the development and growth of last mile delivery providers and participants.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the e-commerce sector grows and online purchases become more prevalent, there is a need to look into a critical gap in the industry for the provision of parcel lockers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Currently, we have multiple players in a fragmented market, with others intending to join in to provide this particular last mile delivery service.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Current parcel locker providers are extremely differentiated and unstandardised.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They vary in terms of business, operations and subscription models, customer interface and even locker size.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As a result, customers and businesses who use parcel lockers face multiple challenges trying to navigate through the variety of particular last mile delivery services.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As mentioned by a few Members – Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Ng Ling Ling – there is a need to look into issues of accessibility for seniors and the less abled, as well as physical and cybersecurity requirements, particularly since we anticipate the sector to grow even further in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the near future, customers using such services should have ease of access, which is to say, there should be sufficient parcel locker locations, making it convenient for customers to receive and collect their parcels in a safe and timely manner.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Currently, the custody of a parcel goes from seller to last mile delivery riders before it ends up with the customer.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the new proposed network, last mile delivery riders may no longer have direct contact with sellers and, instead, deposit parcels into lockers at designated locations.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Therefore, from the moment the parcel departs from the seller until it arrives safely in the hands of the customer, it is essential to protect sellers, last mile delivery riders, customers and Pick Network from wrongful claims in the event of damage to the parcel even whilst in transit.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We must especially keep in mind the delivery riders who currently deliver direct to customers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Customers receive the parcels in good condition and this protects the delivery riders from fraudulent claims.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, with the current proposal, delivery riders will deliver to parcel lockers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we ensure that the delivery riders are protected when the parcel is damaged between the point of him/her completing the delivery to the parcel lockers and the customers retrieving the parcels?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have met a few delivery riders who are exceptionally cautious when delivering parcels and resort to taking pictures of the recipient receiving their parcels to ensure that he/she is safe from any claims of damages to the parcels as such fraudulent claims may pose a significant financial loss to the delivery riders.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Assuming delivery riders earn less than $5 dollars per successful delivery, if a fraudulent claim of a damaged parcel worth $100 is made on him, it will mean he loses his entire income for a day or two.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Thus, we must ensure a robust and reliable system of parcel delivery, with proper recourse, should parcels be damaged or lost.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Notwithstanding the need for a robust and reliable system to safeguard all the stakeholders involved, through the provision of such lockers, the common practice of delivery staff taking pictures of customers receiving parcels or even taking pictures of customers' homes upon delivery of parcel to avoid being unfairly penalised for parcel damage or as proof of delivery, will no longer be necessary.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would be of great benefit in terms of protecting the customers' privacy, too.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Another consideration that we should take note of is that, in the current market, each service provider operates independently, providing their own physical lockers which vary in terms of size and accessibility.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They also often service only their own propriety platform, for example, Ninja Van lockers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If two or more competing service providers are at the same location, such as with Ninja Van and Bluport, it may result in under-utilisation of lockers and inefficient use of space.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is in line with the current trend of co-sharing assets to promote its efficient utilisation, such as that seen on platforms like AirBnB, Grab and MoBike.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Additionally, in locations that experience a high volume of parcel delivery, we can also consider piloting the use of Automated Storage Retrieval Systems (ASRS) that are more volumetrically efficient at storage and has a more efficient physical footprint.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With economies of scale, ASRS may also enable the use of technology to capture the condition of parcels at the point of delivery to ensure that there are no wrongful claims and disagreements between buyer, seller, third party last mile delivery providers and Pick Network.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, delivery companies can do more for the same amount of resource.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There is the potential for less failed delivery and, hence, less wastage on travel times, leading to savings in fuel and operating costs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Consequently, this will also be beneficial for businesses and deliverymen who may only be paid upon successful delivery.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We can also consider an accompanying messaging app to inform recipients that their parcel has been safely delivered at the respective collection points so that they can be retrieved.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The faster the turnaround time for these lockers, the higher the capacity for the network.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With this in mind, will there be a time-bound constraint for the use of these lockers?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Are there any other costs incurred by businesses and customers using this facility?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Beyond costs, there are other considerations to these parcel lockers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will it be limited to only some last mile service providers?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will small businesses or homebased businesses that do their own delivery for costs reasons have equal access to these facilities as it can potentially help with their operations and costs?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How viable is it for us to extend the use of such facilities to them?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we also consider extending this service to parcel pick-ups and parcel returns, too?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is an additional service that is provided by current parcel locker players and I think we should provide such a service, too.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A final consideration would be, with the increased use of packaging, which will inevitably increase with the growth in ecommerce, how do we use these platforms to promote our Green Plan recycling effort?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we have reminder posters at parcel lockers, or else, incentivise the proper disposal and recycling of packaging?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Over the past few years, we have experienced the rapid growth of online shopping.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This increase, as well as advances in technology, has also led to the development and growth of last mile delivery participants.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the e-commerce sector grows and online purchases become more prevalent, there is a need to look into a critical gap in the last-mile delivery industry.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Currently, we have multiple players in a fragmented market, with others intending to join in to provide the service.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the provision of a nationwide parcel locker network, we are able to provide certain standards and guidelines in order to protect customers and businesses.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the establishment of a nationwide parcel locker network, it is also important that we keep in mind how we can protect the delivery riders.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Previously, when the delivery rider delivers directly to the customer, the customer receives the parcels in good condition and this also protects the delivery riders from fraudulent claims.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, with the current proposal, the delivery riders will place the parcel in designated lockers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we ensure the delivery riders are protected when the parcel is damaged between the time when the parcel is placed in the locker to the time when the customer retrieves the parcel?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Thus, we must ensure a robust system of parcel delivery and a claims process that is fair to all parties.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Notwithstanding, with the provision of a nationwide parcel locker network, we can promote a more effective use of space.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It also prevents parcel locker providers from allocating their lockers to specific platforms only.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This can also increase the number of successful deliveries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, the deployment of a nationwide network of parcel lockers in specified premises has many advantages and benefits to businesses, customers and last mile delivery providers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is also a responsive adaptation of our postal service in light of the growth of e-commerce and the decline of mail volume as a result of increased digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With that Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, notwithstanding the clarifications above, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With this option, they do not need to ensure that they are waiting at their residences or offices in order to receive their parcels.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, this arrangement will certainly help provide better service with increased productivity and efficiency.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Parcel lockers will alleviate the problem of manpower shortage in this sector.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): The Bill is comprehensive and ride on other existing legislation to counter mischief and security threats.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share with the House how many such cases have been detected and deterred in the past?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What has the Ministry done and invested in to ensure that our system is robust against security threats?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Government invest more in such security measures and software development?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On one hand, with many transactions now going paperless, the volume of letters sent through the post is decreasing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As one example of this trend, just in December last year, Ikea announced that it will be discontinuing its iconic Ikea paper catalogue after 70 years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On the other hand, parcel deliveries has grown with the booming e-commerce sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A study done in 2020 noted that Singapore's business-to-consumer e-commerce market has been growing at a double-digit rate since 2017.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Already, the growth of e-commerce has strained our postal system which was mainly designed for letters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SingPost attributed the lapses largely to the rise in parcel deliveries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendments to the Postal Services Act are timely for responding to consumer trends.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new public parcel locker network will also help to ease the load on our postmen and postwomen who work tirelessly to ensure that the postal system runs smoothly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, the Bill will introduce a nationwide network of public parcel lockers at HDB estates, public transport hubs and community spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The public parcel locker network is intended to complement commercial parcel locker network in private residential and commercial spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the scope of the public parcel locker network is extensive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This locks the private parcel locker networks out of a significant portion of the market.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a result, this may stifle innovation by the private players.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Private parcel locker operators have been in the market for some period of time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The industry is also fairly competitive with many options available to consumers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With the introduction of the public parcel locker network, how will the Government continue to ensure that both public and private parcel locker network players remains competitive and continues to innovate?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, the new section 23R will allow the Postal authority to open and search a public parcel locker.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will also allow the Postal authority to detain and open any parcel in a public parcel locker.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This, is to mitigate risks to public safety and is consistent with the approach for postal articles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MCI and IMDA have also stated that they will require the operator of the public parcel locker network to put in place security measures including video surveillance and presence sensors in the locker compartments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand this will also include cybersecurity protection measures.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, there is also collaboration with MHA and SCDF to ensure that the locker design and parcel handling meets safety and security requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the powers for the Postal authority in section 23R and the security measures announced for the public parcel locker network do not necessarily apply to the private parcel locker networks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The security risks that threaten the public parcel locker networks similarly apply to private ones.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify what measures will be in place, aside from existing Government powers under other laws, to address security risks for private parcel locker networks?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The intention is to level the playing field for delivery service providers in the last mile delivery market.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, many delivery service providers currently provide parcel tracking services, where the parcels can be tracked throughout the journey.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With Regulated Wholesale Access, the parcels will be handed over to SingPost for the last mile of delivery into the recipients' letter boxes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Without compatible tracking systems between the delivery service providers and SingPost, it may not be possible to track parcels throughout their delivery journey.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was a concern raised by Ninja Van in response to the public consultation for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This would represent a step backwards in terms of the quality of delivery services offered to consumers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may be particularly important given that there is an additional point of handover of the parcels from the delivery service providers to SingPost, which increases the risks of mistakes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, given that there are technologies available on the market to track the delivery of postal articles, is the Ministry or IMDA looking into how tracked deliveries can be made the default in the Postal system?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Right now, consumers have to pay premiums and go through additional processes for the tracked delivery of letters or parcels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the technology is readily available, why not implement it across the board.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The volume of postal articles that go through the postal system will help in spreading out the costs of implementation.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Members' responses and questions fall into two broad themes, namely first, what we are doing to ensure citizens and consumers can fully benefit from the deployment of the nationwide parcel locker network or the "Network"; and two, what we are doing to enable businesses to reap productivity gains from the Network, while safeguarding it against cybersecurity threats.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We note Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Gerald Giam's query about whether there are plans to deploy Pick's lockers at private estates and condominiums.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Parcel lockers can help achieve efficiencies in residential estates with sufficient density, and which are currently under-served.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is why Pick's rollout plan is focused on HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Some private condominiums are already being served by a commercial parcel locker operator, who has agreed to join the Network.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Pick will encourage its partners to expand their deployment wherever feasible, so that more locations, including private condominiums, can be served.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Private estate dwellers, including those who live in less dense estates, which might not be ideal for parcel locker deployment can also benefit from Pick's lockers deployed near them, especially those at public transport nodes and Community Centres or Community Clubs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There was also a question raised by Mr Gerald Giam about the siting of the parcel lockers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Pick will focus on rolling out the Network in areas that will be convenient for the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In looking for ideal locations for these parcel lockers, Pick has taken on feedback from the ground, including all town councils in determining suitable locker sites in HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is also working closely with MOT and LTA to review data such as transport ridership, while taking into account operational, safety and security requirements, to identify suitable locker sites at public transport nodes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Darryl David has also raised a concern about the pricing for parcel locker use.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I should highlight here that the charges for the parcel locker will be charged to the DSPs and the consumer may or may not actually see what these charges are because usually the consumer will interface with the e-commerce marketplace.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And as to how this is then translated into the consumer price, we leave this to the workings of the e-commerce marketplace, the sellers as well as the DSPs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, I should highlight that from Pick's perspective, in order for us to achieve the kind of efficiencies that we envision for the entire urban logistics sector, it stands to reason that the prices offered to the DSPs has to be affordable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
